By decoupling the probabilistic scoring phase from the hard classification phase, practitioners can optimize probability cutoffs to balance sensitivity and specificity according to domain-specific cost functions. This window collectively demonstrates the evolution from rigid statistical assumptions to flexible, computationally intensive algorithms designed to extract signal from noisy, imbalanced, and highly correlated datasets. reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity and leakage vetoes are paramount when integrating these models into live systems. Data leakage often occurs when post-event features inadvertently influence pre-event predictions, artificially inflating AUC metrics during backtesting. Furthermore, severe multicollinearity among biomechanical sensors can cause unstable coefficient estimates in linear discriminants or misleading importance scores in tree ensembles. A rigorous cross-layer veto mechanism must continuously monitor feature correlation matrices and temporal alignment, automatically flagging and isolating predictors that violate causal ordering or introduce redundant information, thereby preserving the integrity of the sovereign primitive outputs.
